Paragraph:
Translation: Only the material body of the indestructible, immeasurable and eternal living entity is subject to destruction; therefore, fight, O descendant of Bharata.

Purport (Excerpt): The material body is perishable by nature. It may perish immediately, or it may do so after a hundred years. It is a question of time only. There is no chance of maintaining it indefinitely... As soon as the spirit soul is out of this material body, the body begins to decompose; therefore it is the spirit soul which maintains this body.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna is paralyzed by the guilt of potentially causing the death of his relatives' bodies.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna reiterates the inevitability of physical death. Whether today in battle or in a hundred years, the body is destined for destruction. He uses this absolute fact to command Arjuna to perform his duty ('therefore, fight').
Outcome/Resolution: Krishna removes the illusion of control Arjuna has over life and death, pushing him toward action based on religious principle rather than sentimentality.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.letting go of Control: Realizing one cannot prevent the inevitable

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Svadharma (One's prescribed occupational duty, which must be executed)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Because the soul is eternal and the body is guaranteed to perish regardless of Arjuna's actions, his hesitation is based on a false sense of control. True religion dictates that he sacrifice the temporary body in the execution of his righteous duty (Dharma).
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This teaches 'radical acceptance.' Arjuna is terrified of being the cause of death. Krishna bluntly points out that physical destruction is a guaranteed biological reality, completely out of Arjuna's ultimate control. By accepting the inevitability of death, the paralyzing anxiety surrounding it diminishes, freeing the individual to act.
